# The split that makes sense, and states read off a history

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`the-split-that-makes-sense` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](the-split-that-makes-sense.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> For a determined law, the coarsest split keeping the map's value and carrying a law makes sense, and part of the value alone makes sense exactly where the rest makes no difference to its next value. Every history of values is a determined law, finite-state exactly where it is eventually periodic.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. With Becoming.Unfolding's definitions: a determined law next read through a map o is the frame Law.frameBy next o; a description makes sense when it identifies exactly the alike configurations, and alike is the same future through the map. (`Becoming.Law.frameBy`, `Becoming.IdentifiesAlike`, `Becoming.identifiesAlike_iff`, `Becoming.Alike`, `Becoming.Law.SameFuture`, `Becoming.Law.alike_iff_sameFuture`)
2. Under a determined law, a description goes alike with the law exactly where it carries what it identifies into what it identifies. A split keeping the map's value and going alike relates configurations by a bisimulation and loses nothing the map takes, and the coarsest such split makes sense. (`Becoming.GoAlike`, `Becoming.Law.goAlike_process_iff`, `Becoming.Bisimulation`, `Becoming.Law.kernel_bisimulation`, `Becoming.Law.sameFuture_of_law`, `Becoming.Law.identifiesAlike_of_law`)
3. The split lumping everything makes sense exactly where the futures through the map are all the same; where the map is the identity, the configuration itself makes sense. (`Becoming.Law.const_identifiesAlike_iff`, `Becoming.Law.whole_identifiesAlike`, `Becoming.identifiesAlike_id_iff`)
4. The map's present value makes sense by itself exactly where it fixes its own future through the map, exactly where it goes alike with the law, a condition on one step. (`Becoming.Law.now_identifiesAlike_iff`, `Becoming.Law.sameFuture_of_goAlike`, `Becoming.Law.now_identifiesAlike_iff_goAlike`)
5. For a law on pairs (x, c) whose map takes the first part, the first part alone makes sense exactly where the rest makes no difference to its next value, equivalently where the rest never makes a difference through the map; where the next value is set by a rule changing with it, next (x, c) = (F c x, G c x), exactly where F c x = F c′ x for every x, c and c′, the condition of adaptive_state_law_iff of Becoming.Mechanism. (`Becoming.Law.part_identifiesAlike_iff_step`, `Becoming.Law.part_identifiesAlike_iff`, `Becoming.Law.adaptive_identifiesAlike_iff`, `Becoming.adaptive`, `Becoming.adaptive_state_law_iff`)
6. Motion.move (x, v) = (x + v, v) is an adaptive process; with a map taking x, the pair makes sense, x alone carries no law, v alone loses x, and neither alone makes sense; under the still law, x alone makes sense. (`Becoming.Motion.cancel`, `Becoming.Motion.move`, `Becoming.Motion.move_adaptive`, `Becoming.Motion.pair_identifiesAlike`, `Becoming.Motion.standing_alone`, `Becoming.Motion.passing_alone`, `Becoming.Motion.neither_alone`, `Becoming.Motion.still`, `Becoming.Motion.orbit_still`, `Becoming.Motion.still_identifiesAlike`)
7. In a sequence of values o, moments t and t′ are one state when o (t + n) = o (t′ + n) for every n. This is an equivalence that goes on as itself, it is the same future through the map read along an orbit, and where every moment takes a different value each moment is its own state. (`Becoming.SameAhead`, `Becoming.SameAhead.refl`, `Becoming.SameAhead.symm`, `Becoming.SameAhead.trans`, `Becoming.SameAhead.next`, `Becoming.sameAhead_orbit_iff`, `Becoming.SameAhead.new_each`)
8. Every history of values is a determined law read through a map: under the law of moments, each going on to the next, two moments are alike exactly where they are one state. (`Becoming.alike_moments_iff`, `Becoming.Law.frameBy`)
9. A pigeonhole up to a relation, with no decision, gives: a history of values has finitely many states (every moment one state with some moment below some L) exactly where two of its moments are one state. A configuration that returns has finitely many states through every map. (`Becoming.split_top`, `Becoming.shared_below`, `Becoming.StatesBelow`, `Becoming.statesBelow_of_same`, `Becoming.finitely_many_states_iff`, `Becoming.Law.Returns.states`, `Becoming.Law.Returns`)
10. The course of the two-valued negation has exactly two states: moments 0 and 1 differ (through revision_never_rests of Becoming.Diagonal), moments 0 and 2 are one state, and every moment is one of the two, each defined through the other. (`Becoming.Negation.course`, `Becoming.Negation.zero_two`, `Becoming.Negation.two_states`, `Becoming.Negation.each_through_other`, `Becoming.Diagonal.revision_never_rests`, `Becoming.Diagonal.flip_moves`)
11. Law.goAlike_process_iff is the instance of Becoming.Learning's goAlike_iff_lumped, written independently with the same proof. Learning's lasso from moment i with period q + 1 holds exactly where moments i and i + (q + 1) are one state, so there are finitely many states exactly where there is a lasso. (`Becoming.Learning.goAlike_iff_lumped`, `Becoming.Law.goAlike_process_iff`, `Becoming.Learning.Lasso`, `Becoming.lasso_iff_sameAhead`, `Becoming.finitely_many_states_iff_lasso`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No premise: Law.now_identifiesAlike_iff_goAlike, Law.part_identifiesAlike_iff_step, alike_moments_iff and finitely_many_states_iff are two-way and hold for every determined law, map or sequence.
- Law.identifiesAlike_of_law needs the split to keep the map's value, go alike with the law and be coarsest; Law.Returns.states needs the configuration to return (local conditions).
- The law of moments uses only the succession of steps, the representation's shared step index (a commitment of the representation); no law beyond it is given.
- Only determined laws are stated; frames that branch are stated by Becoming.Unfolding's Alike.
- That a description making sense exists as values (a name for each class) is not stated; the classes always exist as relations (SameFuture, SameAhead).

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That a description making sense exists as values is not stated: naming in general needs a quotient (Quot.sound).
- Whether a finite prefix fixes the states is not stated here (see Becoming.Learning).
- In alike_moments_iff the determinacy of the law of moments is trivial; the content is that likeness is being one state. Witness: `Becoming.alike_moments_iff`.
- It does not show that any actual unfolding has finitely many states.
- **Counterexample:** Carrying a law is not enough for sense: the split lumping everything always carries one (goAlike_const) and makes sense only where all futures through the map are the same (Law.const_identifiesAlike_iff); in Motion the standing alone carries no law and the passing alone loses the standing (Motion.neither_alone). <a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Answering Ren's “what is that "make sense" itself? what makes a pair, a pair?” and “maybe change(now) -> future”: relative to the map, the split that makes sense is unique and given by the law; two are a pair exactly where the law does not split between them and the map tells them apart. It tests Ren's speculation (“the full "truth" can be derived, situationally, including the cognition/controller part”): a situational truth is exact, and includes the controller exactly where it makes a difference through the map (Law.adaptive_identifiesAlike_iff). It answers whether an unfolding has a law: every history of values is the law of moments, the content of a law is its compression, and finitely many states is repetition from some moment on. This is the deterministic case of the minimal automaton and of the causal states of computational mechanics. The one-step forms come from a review by the owner of Becoming.Mechanism. Readings (the AI's, adopted on Ren's delegation; Ren agreed with the reply containing them): 阴阳 as the standing and the passing, and as the negation's two states; change and state each defined through the other.
